## Maintenance notes

- A challenge's `extras`/`module_preludes` tables carry elaboration context
  (attribute commands, `CoeFun` instances, `variable`/`open` blocks) that the
  kernel closure cannot see.  Extend them if regeneration produces compile
  errors in that challenge's `Challenge.lean`; the assembler fails loudly if one
  of the challenge's own table keys no longer matches any extracted
  declaration.  The tables are per challenge, so an LDT key never constrains the
  QPBT closure or the other way round.
- A `module_preludes` entry is one scope, or a list of scopes each covering a
  line range (`first`/`last`) of its module: a module needs one scope per source
  section whose context differs.  A scope opened with `noncomputable section` in
  the source is marked `"noncomputable": true`, because the definitions inside
  such a section carry no `noncomputable` keyword of their own.
- The target statements in each footer mirror the theorems in the library:
  `challenge_footer.lean` mirrors
  `MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/MainTheorem/MainFormal.lean`, and
  `challenge_qpbt_footer.lean` mirrors
  `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Completeness.lean`,
  `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/LowDegreeGameTheorems.lean`,
  `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness.lean`, and
  `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/QubitForm.lean`.  If a library statement changes, update
  the footer too - comparator fails with "theorem statement do not match" until
  the two agree.
- Declarations without a source range (compiler-generated congruence lemmas
  and `autoParam` helpers) are emitted as explanatory comments; they
  regenerate identically during elaboration of the challenge file.
- A configured header or footer file that is not in the tree is reported and
  omitted, so a challenge under development can be generated before its footer
  exists.  That omission is confined to `--write`: `--update` refuses such a
  challenge rather than checking in a copy without that part.
- A closure declaration cannot be `private`: a private name is qualified by its
  defining module, so the challenge file could never re-declare it under the
  library's name.  Closure members found to be private are made public in the
  library (see `docs/comparator.md`, "Environment alignment").


## Split (multi-module) challenges

A challenge whose JSON configuration sets `"split": true` is generated as one
Mathlib-only module per contributing library module instead of one file:

```
python3 scripts/comparator/assemble_challenge.py <closure.tsv> \
    --root . --challenge qpbt --split-dir <out>
```

`<out>/Challenge.lean` imports the parts under `<out>/Challenge/<library
path>.lean` and carries the header and the `sorry`-ed target statements; each
part imports Mathlib plus the mirrors of the library modules its source module
imports.  The layout is what makes Lean generate the same auxiliary
declarations, under the same names, as the library — see the "environment
alignment" section of `docs/comparator.md`.  The checked-in copy is a
directory, and `check_challenge_drift.py --challenge <name> [--update]`
compares or rewrites the whole tree.

    """Assembled body text; raises ``StaleContextTables`` on an unmatched key."""

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("tsv", type=Path, help="TSV from extract_closure.lean")
    parser.add_argument(

        type=Path,

        type=Path,
        default=None,
        help="write one challenge module per library module into this directory",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    try:
        challenge = load_challenges([args.challenge])[0]
        if args.split_dir is not None:
            files = assemble_split(challenge, args.root, args.tsv)
            for rel, text in sorted(files.items()):

                dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                dest.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")

            return 0

    except (ChallengeConfigError, StaleContextTables) as exc:

Issue #662: make the local comparator accept the QPBT challenge.

**It now does.** In the challenge repository
[Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator](https://github.com/Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator)
(branch `draft-challenge`), pinned at this PR's head:

```
$ ./verify.sh --fake-landrun
...
Lean default kernel accepts the solution
Your solution is okay!
exit 0   —   5 min 44 s wall, peak RSS 5.3 GiB
```

(Three independent runs of the same script: 5m04s at the pre-merge pin, 7m53s
at `4aec9ebe`, 5m44s at the final head, all `exit 0`.)  That single verdict
covers, with the official `leanprover/comparator` binary for toolchain
`v4.32.0`:

* the statements of `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` and
  `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit` are identical in the Mathlib-only
  challenge and in this library;
* every constant in their kernel closure matches **including values and
  proofs** (comparator compares the full `ConstantInfo`);
* the axiom closure is within `propext`, `Quot.sound`, `Classical.choice`;
* the whole solution environment replays through the Lean kernel.

Before this PR's new commit the same run rejected. Round 1 (K6) fixed one
class and reached `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_fixed_field_model`; this round
replaced the one-mismatch-per-run loop with a systematic diff and closed all

## The diagnosis

A diagnostic copy of comparator — its compare loop collecting every
mismatching closure constant instead of throwing on the first, and reporting
the first differing subterm — showed **26** mismatches, in three families with
a single root cause:

* Lean caches an abstracted nested proof and a `match` auxiliary **per
  module**, keyed by the statement, and names it after whichever declaration of
  that module first needed it.
* Instance synthesis inside a module only sees what that module's imports
  declare.

A single-file challenge can therefore neither reproduce an auxiliary name when
the library needs the same fact in two modules, nor keep an instance out of
scope. Concretely:

| # | family | challenge had | library has |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | instance visibility in `Algebra/FieldBasis.lean`, `Algebra/SelfDualBasis.lean` | `MIPStarRE.Quantum.instNeZeroTwo` | `@Nat.instNeZeroSucc 1` |
| 4 | matcher naming | `instReprPauliKind.repr.match_1` (from `Algebra/Pauli.lean`) | `pauliPointBlock.match_1` (from `Test/PauliBasisTest.lean`) |
| 12 | nested-proof naming | `conjIsometry._proof_1`, `._proof_2` (from `QPBT/State.lean`) | `applyOperatorToState._proof_*`, `eprState._proof_1`, `idealState._proof_2`, `idealQubitState._proof_2`, in five modules |

Two of those ten looked like a different problem in round 1 —
`exists_fixed_field_model` and `exists_self_dual_normal_basis_gal` differ in
their **proof terms**, not their statements — but the first differing subterm
has exactly the same shape (`const` versus `app`), so they are the same cause.

## The fix

The QPBT challenge is generated as **one Mathlib-only module per contributing
library module**, mirroring the source path
(`Challenge/MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Pauli.lean`, …), each importing Mathlib and
the mirrors of the library modules its own source module imports, with
`Challenge.lean` importing them all and stating the targets with `sorry`.
Every auxiliary is then created in the mirror of the module that creates it in
the library, and gets the same name by construction; instance visibility
matches by construction too. All 26 mismatches disappear with that change
alone.

**No Lean library file is touched by the new commit.** No statement,
definition body or proof script changes, and the solution environment is
bit-identical to the one this PR already published. Only the generator, its
configuration, its tests, the checked-in generated copy and the prose change.

* `scripts/comparator/assemble_challenge.py` — `--split-dir`, a
  `SplitAssembler` reusing the existing namespace/prelude machinery, transitive
  local-import closure and minimal mirror imports.
* `scripts/comparator/challenges.py` — `split` and `common_opens`; `qpbt` sets
  `split=True`.
* `scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py` — tree comparison and
  `--update` for split challenges.
* `scripts/comparator/expected/ChallengeQPBT.lean.expected` →
  `scripts/comparator/expected/qpbt/` (21 files).
* `scripts/tests/test_comparator_challenge_drift.py` — the configuration test
  accepts a directory, plus a new guard that the QPBT challenge stays split and
  that every challenge module imports only Mathlib and other challenge modules.
* `docs/comparator.md`, `scripts/comparator/README.md`, the challenge header.

The LDT challenge is untouched and still regenerates byte-identically.

## Carried over from round 1

`MIPStarRE.Quantum.instNeZeroTwo` and
`MIPStarRE.Quantum.instRingHomInvPairIdComplex` (commit `c2c1b478`) are
statement-preserving named instances added when a single-file challenge was
still assumed. With the mirrored partition neither is needed for acceptance,
and `instRingHomInvPairIdComplex` is never selected by synthesis at all (the
goal carries the `RCLike`-derived `Semiring ℂ` path), so it does not appear in
the closure. Reverting them rebuilds most of the Quantum and QPBT trees, so it
is left for a follow-up issue rather than folded in here.
